decisions.reason: The title identifies the intended application, not an additional charged-equation conclusion. Step 1.1 proves the cube Poincare bound by coordinate integration and H1 closure; steps 1.2 and 2.1 prove both directions of the C1 zero-boundary characterization by graph-layer approximation and the local boundary L2 estimate. These are exactly the Statement claims and require no charged source.

The cited bump supplier proof 1.1 constructs rho(x)=sigma((s^2-sum x_j^2)/(s^2-r^2)); this is explicitly radial, nonnegative, smooth, one on the inner ball and supported in the outer ball. Taking its complement and rescaling gives precisely the cutoff and derivative bounds in F5 and step 2.1. The cancellation formula, inner flux -delta_ij/3, near/far Holder split and radius scaling are consistent with -Delta N g=g. No radialization assumption is missing.

The actual bump supplier constructs a smooth function of sum x_j^2 in every dimension, so normalization produces the radial mollifiers and harmonic averaging kernels of F2. Step 3.1 supplies the normal-normal boundary jet of the lift; step 4.1 removes the forcing trace before odd reflection. The even radial cutoff in step 5.1 preserves oddness, and the mean-value convolution in step 6.1 yields the interior harmonic derivative bounds. The stated suppliers license these choices.

F2 invokes a theorem whose explicit Countable Choice hypothesis was absent from both this Statement and its problem Definition. The final step needs Banachness under the cited Banach-space derivative definitions; no local completeness proof discharged that premise. Added Countable Choice to Statement, Given, A1, deps and its role, and made its exact completeness use explicit in F2 and step 3.1. The algebraic remainder and derivative formula are preserved.

F9 omitted the bounded W(k,2)-extension-domain hypothesis and no direct supplier established it. This is a routine missing prerequisite check on the ball, rather than a failure of the smoothness conclusion. Added the exact extension theorem and definitions as dependencies, stated its AC hypothesis in F12, and proved the ball has smooth one-sided sphere graphs in step 1.1. Thus every integer-order embedding/algebra use in step 2.2 has its domain hypothesis. The Example section and its complete smooth constrained-data conclusion are unchanged.
